title: You don't need a telescope to photograph the Milky Way
alt: A star-filled night sky with the band of the Milky Way, above dark rocks and the corner of a building.

posts.facebook:
Here's a surprise: you don't need a telescope to photograph the Milky Way.

Put a camera on a tripod and leave the shutter open long enough, and it records stars your eyes can barely make out.

A beginners' course, or an evening at a dark-sky site, will teach you the settings. Bring the camera you already have, a tripod and a red head torch (a headlamp, in the US). A local astronomy society can point you to dark sites.

Have you ever seen the Milky Way with your own eyes?

How to start, and where to go → https://dontdieretired.com/list/learn-astrophotography/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=things-to-do
